simple.meaning: בָּקַק (bâqaq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to pour out, i.e. to empty , figuratively, to depopulate ; by analogy, to spread out (as a fruitful vine).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 9 times across Isaiah, Jeremiah, Hosea, Nahum, beginning at Isaiah 19:3. Its contexts include Egypt, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּקַק (H1238).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: בָּקַק (bâqaq) / H1238 is traced through Isaiah 19:3, Isaiah 24:1, Isaiah 24:3, Jeremiah 19:7 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The spirit of Egypt will fail within it. I will destroy its counsel. They will seek the idols, the charmers, those who have familiar spirits, and the wizards.

timeline.evidenceText: The spirit of Egypt will fail within it. I will destroy its counsel. They will seek the idols, the charmers, those who have familiar spirits, and the wizards.
Behold, Yahweh makes the earth empty, makes it waste, turns it upside down, and scatters its inhabitants.
The earth will be utterly emptied and utterly laid waste; for Yahweh has spoken this word.
The earth will be utterly emptied and utterly laid waste; for Yahweh has spoken this word.

“ ‘ “I will make the counsel of Judah and Jerusalem void in this place. I will cause them to fall by the sword before their enemies, and by the hand of those who seek their life. I will give their dead bodies to be food for the birds of the sky and for the animals of the earth.
I will send to Babylon strangers, who will winnow her.
Israel is a luxuriant vine that produces his fruit.
The shield of his mighty men is made red. The valiant men are in scarlet. The chariots flash with steel in the day of his preparation, and the pine spears are brandished.

definitions.short: to pour out, i.e. to empty , figuratively, to depopulate ; by analogy, to spread out (as a fruitful vine)
definitions.full: H1238. baqaq I. [ בָּקַק ] verb be luxuriant (Arabic be profuse, abundant (see especially Conjugations I. IV, Lane)) — Qal Participle בֹּקֵק luxuriant Hosea 10:1 (figurative of Israel as vine). II. [ בָּקַק ] verb empty (compare probably Arabic make a gurgling noise , of a mug dipped in water, or emptied of water) — Qal Perfect וּבַקֹּתִ֫י Jer 19:7 , בָּֽקֲקוּ Nahum 2:3 ; Participle בּוֺקֵק Isa 24:1 , בִּקֲקִים Nahum 2:3 ; empty, lay waste land, accusative, Isa 24:1 ; Nahum 2:3 , also absolute 2:3 ; figurative make void (object עֵצָה ) Jer 19:7 . Niph`al Perfect וְנָָֽבְקָה (compare Ges § 67 , R. 11) Isa 19:3 ; Imperfect 3feminine singular תִּבּוֺק 24:3 ; Infinitive absolute הִבּוֺק 24:3 ; — be emptied (laid waste) 24:3 תִבּוֺק הִבּוֺק , of land (|| תִּבּוֺז הִבּוֺז ); figurative of spirit, courage 19:3 . Po. Imperfect יְבֹקֲקוּ Jer 51:2 empty out (devastate) land.
